lessons.title: How MLS is built
lessons.objective: You can explain MLS structure and why there is no relegation.

payload.prompt: What makes MLS different from most world leagues?

options.text: It has promotion and relegation
It is a closed league with a salary cap and no relegation
Players own their own teams

explanation.correct: Exactly. MLS is a closed league: the same clubs stay in, and a salary cap keeps spending in check, so there is no relegation drama.
explanation.incorrect: MLS is a closed league with a salary cap and no promotion or relegation. Clubs stay in whatever their results.
explanation.sayThisLine: MLS is closed, so nobody gets relegated.

payload.prompt: Match the MLS term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: No promotion or relegation: clubs keep their place from year to year.
The trophy for the best regular-season record, separate from the MLS Cup.
A star whose pay can sit above the normal salary-cap limit.

explanation.summary: MLS pairs a closed structure with a salary cap, and uses Designated Players to make room for stars.
explanation.sayThisLine: The cap keeps things balanced; Designated Players are the exception.

payload.template: The {{shield}} goes to the best regular-season team, while the {{cup}} is decided in the {{format}}.

explanation.correct: Right. The Shield rewards the best regular season and the MLS Cup is won in the playoffs. Inter Miami won the 2025 MLS Cup, beating Vancouver 3-1.
explanation.incorrect: The Supporters' Shield rewards the best regular-season record. The MLS Cup is a playoff trophy, often won by a team that did not finish first.

statement.speaker: Alex
statement.text: There's no relegation in MLS, so mid-table isn't dangerous.

payload.question: What does he mean?

options.text: Finishing in the middle of the table is safe
Teams can't be dropped to a lower division
Mid-table teams are guaranteed playoffs
Losing matches has no consequences

payload.translation: In most leagues, finishing near the bottom means demotion. MLS has no relegation, so even a last-place team stays in MLS next season.

followUps.line: Does that make the league less competitive?
followUps.why: Opens a strategic discussion about parity vs stakes.

followUps.line: So teams can't be demoted at all?
followUps.why: Confirms the structural difference from other leagues.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you're used to Premier League or La Liga, the lack of relegation is genuinely different; it's fine to ask about it.

payload.prompt: MLS has promotion and relegation, just like the Premier League. True or false?

scene.alt: A league table with no drop zone marked at the bottom, showing MLS clubs staying in the league.

explanation.correct: False. MLS is a closed league, so even the last-place club is back next season.
explanation.incorrect: MLS has no promotion or relegation. It is a closed league, which is very different from the Premier League.

lessons.title: The salary cap and Designated Players
lessons.objective: You can explain how MLS balances stars and the salary cap.

payload.prompt: Why does MLS have a salary cap?

options.text: To limit player wages everywhere
To balance competition and keep teams from overspending
Because American law requires it

explanation.correct: Right. The salary cap keeps spending close between teams, so rich clubs can't buy their way to dominance every year.
explanation.incorrect: MLS's salary cap exists to create league parity by preventing the richest owners from building super-teams that always win.
explanation.sayThisLine: The cap keeps the league balanced, so any team can compete if they're smart.

payload.prompt: A star forward wants MLS, but his wage is far above the cap limit. What now?

situation.narrative: MLS wants world-class stars but uses a salary cap to keep the league balanced.

facts.label: Player wage
facts.value: Far above the normal per-player limit

options.label: The club uses a Designated Player slot for him
options.consequence: MLS gets a star and the cap rules still protect the other clubs.
considerations: Designated Player slots exist for exactly this situation
Only a limited number of these slots exist per club

options.label: The club tries to fit him in with allocation money
options.consequence: This helps for players a little above the limit, but a true superstar wage needs a Designated Player slot.
considerations: Allocation money can lower a player's cap hit within league rules
It does not stretch to any wage

options.label: The league blocks the deal to keep the cap pure
options.consequence: MLS would keep the cap intact but lose the star power it is trying to attract.
considerations: MLS created Designated Players so this deal could happen

payload.expertNote: The Designated Player rule is MLS's compromise between cap balance and star power.

payload.prompt: Match the money concept to how MLS uses it.

pairs.definition: A limit on what clubs can spend on player pay, to keep the league balanced.
A star whose pay can go above the standard limit, in a limited number of slots.
Funds a club can use to lower a player's cap charge, within league rules.

explanation.summary: The cap creates balance, Designated Players make room for stars, and allocation money adds flexibility.
explanation.sayThisLine: Cap, Designated Players, allocation money: MLS balancing balance with star power.

statement.speaker: Jordan
statement.text: Messi is a Designated Player, but most of the squad counts against the cap.

payload.question: What is the point?

options.text: A star can be signed above the cap limit while the rest of the squad fits under it
Designated Players are an exception to how the cap normally works
Every player is treated exactly the same under the cap
Regular players are not allowed to join MLS

payload.translation: The Designated Player rule lets a club pay a superstar above the normal limit, while the rest of the squad still counts against the salary cap.

followUps.line: Has that worked to attract big names?
followUps.why: Invites her to talk about the stars who have come to MLS.

followUps.line: Does it make some squads top-heavy?
followUps.why: Asks about the trade-off between star power and depth.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you are not sure how the cap works, it is fair to ask how the league stays balanced.

payload.template: A club's pay is limited by the {{cap}}, but a few {{stars}} can earn more through {{exception}}.

explanation.correct: Right. The salary cap applies to the squad, but Designated Player slots let a few stars sit above it.
explanation.incorrect: MLS caps club spending on pay overall, but each club has a limited number of Designated Player slots for stars.

lessons.title: The calendar shift and supporters
lessons.objective: You can explain the 2027 calendar shift and supporter culture.

payload.prompt: When does MLS change its calendar from spring-summer to August-May?

options.text: Already done in 2026
Starting in 2027-28, after a transition season in early 2027
In 2028 after the Olympics

explanation.correct: Exactly. MLS runs a short transition season from February to May 2027, then moves to August-to-May from 2027-28, with a winter break.
explanation.incorrect: MLS is shifting to match the European August-to-May calendar. A transition season in early 2027 bridges the change, and 2027-28 becomes the new standard.

statement.speaker: Casey
statement.text: MLS is moving to the European calendar from 2027, so we line up with everyone else.

payload.question: What does this change?

options.text: MLS now plays August to May like Europe
The 2026 World Cup will be played during the season
National team players have a better international break alignment
MLS seasons will be shorter

payload.translation: Moving to an August-to-May season puts MLS in step with most of the world: transfer windows, international breaks and the Champions League calendar all line up better.

followUps.line: Will that make it easier for US players internationally?
followUps.why: Shows you understand the strategic benefit.

followUps.line: Does the weather matter for the new schedule?
followUps.why: Asks about climate in Canada and the northern US during spring.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If the timing seems odd, it's fair to ask why the league didn't shift sooner.

payload.prompt: An MLS club wants to build supporter culture like European teams. What's the best approach?

situation.narrative: The club has a new stadium and wants to attract passionate fans.

facts.label: Goal
facts.value: Build atmosphere like European clubs with tifos and chants

options.label: Invest in supporters' groups and back their identity
options.consequence: The club builds passionate fan base and lasting atmosphere.
considerations: MLS clubs thrive when supporters organize with the club's backing. Tifo groups and identity matter.

options.label: Hire European staff to teach fans how to build supporter culture
options.consequence: The club gets expert guidance, but culture needs local growth.
considerations: Helpful background knowledge, but authentic supporter culture grows locally from passionate fans, not hired help.

options.label: Ban organized supporter groups to keep stadium family-friendly
options.consequence: The stadium stays quiet and the club loses loyalty-building energy.
considerations: That would kill the culture the club is trying to build. Supporters are the lifeblood of modern clubs.

payload.expertNote: Successful MLS clubs support their fan base: tifo groups, chants and organized seating create lasting atmosphere and identity.

payload.prompt: Match the supporter term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A large coordinated banner or display by organised supporters.
The most passionate organised supporters, often leading chants and displays.
An organised fan group that stands together; Portland's Timbers Army is a famous MLS example.

explanation.summary: Modern supporter culture is built on coordinated displays, loud groups and organised fans.
explanation.sayThisLine: Tifos, ultras, supporters' groups: that is the heart of the atmosphere.

payload.title: Supporting an MLS club
payload.setting: She's excited about her MLS club's growing supporter base.

exchanges.theirMessage: Our tifo group just did an amazing display, the whole corner sang for the whole match.

replies.text: That's what builds a real club culture. Did you plan it together?
replies.theirResponse: Weeks in advance. The ultras organize everything.
replies.coachNote: Shows you know supporters are the foundation.

replies.text: MLS doesn't have real supporter culture.
replies.theirResponse: Are you serious? Watch us play.
replies.coachNote: Dismissing something she loves won't land.

payload.closingNote: She is proud of her supporters' group and the atmosphere they create.
